# ECON 0100 | Vignette E3 | Monopoly

*Vignettes are a certificate of the work done together in Recitation. Due in Recitation.*

The Cauldron Co. is the only firm selling traditional cauldrons. It faces the whole market’s demand, $P = 70 - Q$, so its marginal revenue is $MR = 70 - 2Q$.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

### Q1 | Cauldron Co.

Initially, the Cauldron Co. has high fixed cost, and a low constant marginal cost of $MC = 10$.

a\) Graph and calculate the firm’s profit max quantity ($q^*$).\
b\) Graph and calculate the firm’s profit max price ($P^*$).\
c\) Graph and calculate the firm’s maximal profit ($\pi^*$) if $ATC^* = 20$.\
d\) Graph and calculate the socially efficient quantity.\
e\) Graph and calculate the monopolist’s DWL.

 

 

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::

::::

### Q2 | Taxing The Cauldron Monopoly

To attempt to mitigate the issue of monopoly DWL, the Ministry of Magic decides taxes every cauldron 20 coins, raising Cauldron Co.’ marginal cost to: $MC = 30$.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

a\) Graph and calculate $q^*$ and $P^*$ after the new cost.\
b\) Graph and calculate $\pi^*$ after the new cost if $ATC^* = 45$.\
c\) How much does price rise due to the tax?\
d\) How much does the Ministry collect from this tax?\
e\) Calculate the DWL after the tax.

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::

::::

### Q3 | Lump Sum Tax

Instead, a recent economics graduate proposes a lump sum tax of 600 coins on The Cauldron Co. instead of the tax on each cauldron. Its fixed costs rise while its marginal cost stays at $MC = 10$.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

a\) Graph and calculate $q^*$ and $P^*$ after the lump sum tax.\
b\) Graph and calculate $\pi^*$ after the lump sum tax if $ATC^* = 40$.\
c\) How much does price rise due to the lump sum tax?\
d\) Calculate the DWL after the lump sum tax.\
e\) How much does the Ministry collect under this tax.\
f\) Which tax is better for buyers?

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::

::::

 

# ECON 0100 | Vignette E4 | Duopoly

Orignially Cauldron Co. makes substantial profits as the only seller of traditional cauldrons. This profit draws in a rival with the same costs: high fixed costs and a constant marginal cost of $MC = 10$. They sell into the same market, so $P = 70 - (q_C + q_R)$, where $q_C$ is The Cauldron Co.’s quantity and $q_R$ is its rival’s. The Cauldron Co.’s marginal revenue is $MR_C = 70 - 2q_C - q_R$. This market is symmetric.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

### Q1 | Two Cauldron Makers

a\) Find and graph both firms’ best responses. \
b\) Calculate and graph the Nash equilibrium quantities. \
c\) Calculate the Nash equilibrium price in this market.\
d\) Calculate each firm’s profit if $ATC^* = 25$.\
e\) How does this equilibrium compare to the monopoly equilibrium in Vignette E3? 

:::

::: {.column width=40%}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){width=100%}

:::
